late_notes.text: Infrastructure fix before any bench result: trial chains of Londrina (base and A1) raised a code error and were rerun after the fix. Both results are kept.
late_notes.file: pipeline/engine/chain.py (run_season, new _fallow_piece and FALLOW_PIECE_DAYS); test in tests/test_engine_chain.py
late_notes.cause: RuntimeError 'expected 1 season in instance, got 2' (chain.py, run_season). In Londrina with the real-year climate the warm-up soybean 2019/20 (rain-rule sowing 2019-09-03) died on 2019-09-16 and the warm-up corn sown after it died on 2019-11-03, so the next instance ran from 2019-11-04 to the rain-rule sowing on 2020-12-03, a fallow longer than a year. OSPy places plantings by month and day and built two seasons in that instance. The dead canopies and the September corn are engine outcomes and were not changed.
late_notes.fix: When an instance starts on or before the previous anniversary of its sowing, the fallow up to that anniversary runs first as bare soil in consecutive OSPy pieces of at most 300 days, each carrying the soil water of the day before, every day with its water balance, no reset; each piece checks that no day holds a crop. The crop instance follows from the next day and the pieces join its accounting. Instances shorter than a year run exactly as before. No parameter, date, sowing rule or protocol value changed.
late_notes.proof: Floresta and Cafelandia (base, A1, P1) and Londrina P1 rerun after the fix: every CSV identical to the run before the fix once the two wall-clock columns (init_seconds, seconds) are removed (sha256 per file in data/bench/superseded/, proof_sha256.txt); artifacts.json identical for all 24 regimes. Londrina base: water balance residual at most 2.4e-11 mm over the 473-day instance, handover gap 0. Regression test on synthetic weather: a corn that dies after emergence, then a fallow of almost two years, raised before the fix and passes after.
late_notes.superseded: data/bench/superseded/ (the runs before the fix, with chains.log)
